standard_prerequisites.name: Comparability graph of a partially ordered set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given a partially ordered set, its comparability graph has the elements as vertices and an undirected edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding elements are comparable; the article's own description is retained at source lines 117-120.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the class of graphs into which the proof must partition the edge set of the interval graph, namely two edge-disjoint comparability subgraphs.

standard_prerequisites.name: The partition number p(G)
standard_prerequisites.statement: p(G) is the minimum m such that the edge set of G is the union of m edge-disjoint comparability subgraphs of G; retained at source line 128, together with the covering number c(G) at source line 129.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem asserts p(G) <= 2, so the parameter and its edge-disjointness requirement must be fixed before the statement can be read.

standard_prerequisites.name: Interval graph and unit interval graph
standard_prerequisites.statement: A graph is an interval graph when it is the intersection graph of a system of closed intervals of a line, and a unit interval graph when the intervals all have length one; the article's own definitions are retained at source lines 272-273.
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the graph G of the counted theorem with the intersection graph G_U of a system U of unit intervals, which is the object the proof partitions.

core_obligations: Let U be the system of unit intervals whose intersection graph is G, and run the greedy sweep: take the interval I_1 = [a_1,b_1] of U with the leftmost right endpoint and let X_1 be the set of intervals of U containing b_1 (source lines 285-287).

Continue recursively: if I_1,...,I_k and X_1,...,X_k are defined and intervals remain, choose among the remaining intervals the one with the leftmost right endpoint as I_{k+1} = [a_{k+1},b_{k+1}] and define X_{k+1} as the set of intervals outside the union of the X_i that contain b_{k+1}; the procedure ends after m steps with the X_i partitioning U (source lines 288-291).

Define H_1 as the set of edges of the interval graph G_U whose two intervals lie in the same X_i; since each X_i meets pairwise, H_1 is a union of m vertex-disjoint complete graphs and hence a comparability graph (source lines 293-295).

Define H_2 as the remaining edges, those whose end intervals lie in different X_i-s; using that U consists of unit intervals, show that such an edge must join an interval of X_i to an interval of X_{i+1} for some i, so that H_2 is a bipartite graph (source lines 296-299).
Conclude that H_1 and H_2 are edge-disjoint comparability graphs whose union is the whole edge set, so p(G_U) <= 2 (source line 300).

proof_roadmap.step: Greedily order the unit intervals by leftmost right endpoint and build the consecutive classes X_1,...,X_m that partition U.
Put all edges inside a single class X_i into H_1 and identify H_1 as a union of vertex-disjoint complete graphs.
Put the remaining edges into H_2 and use the unit length hypothesis to show that they only join consecutive classes, so H_2 is bipartite.
Conclude that the two edge-disjoint comparability graphs partition E(G_U).

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Theorem unit（源 281-282 行，证明 285-300 行，共 16 行）：对单位区间图 G 证明 p(G)<=2，即把边集剖成两个可比图。关键操作有两处不是例行核验：一是必须设计出正确的贪心分组，按最右端点最靠左的顺序依次取 I_{k+1} 并把「含 b_{k+1} 且尚未分组」的区间收进 X_{k+1}（285-291 行），这个选择顺序正是让同组区间两两相交、从而 H_1 成为顶点不交的完全图之并的原因；二是必须用「区间长度均为 1」这一假设证明不同组的相交边只能发生在相邻两组之间（298-299 行），这一步是 H_2 为二部图的关键，若区间长度任意则结论不成立。原文位置在证明的 288-291 行与 298-299 行。
